transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just keep seeing it. Out of nowhere, I'll be in the church office, just trying to work, and suddenly I'm back there. I see my cousin on the pavement. I can hear the shouting, see the lights... it's like it's happening all over again. It's hard to act normal when that keeps happening.
When these memories come back, do they feel like something you can't control, or do they seem more like something that just happens to you without warning?

Yeah... without warning. Like I was saying, it just hits me out of nowhere. I'll just be standing there in the church office, trying to act normal, and... the whole scene just comes back. I can't really control it.
Since that incident with your cousin, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah... I suppose I do. I, um... I take the long way around town now. Just so I don't have to pass the community center, or... or that court. 

And if somebody starts talking about that night, I just... I shut it down. Or I find a reason to excuse myself and leave. I just don't want to be around it.
Since the incident with your cousin, have you noticed that you often feel afraid, guilty, or upset when you think about it?

Yeah... I guess you could say that. It's, um... most days it's just sitting there in my chest the second I wake up. Just... this mix of fear and anger. And... guilt. 

I just feel like I... like I failed God. And my family. And the kids who trusted me. It's... yeah. I don't really like talking about that part.
Have these feelings of guilt, fear, and anger been constant since the incident, or do they come and go?
It's... pretty much constant. It's been that way for a long time. Ever since... since he was killed. That was two years and three months ago.
